subject: Highlighting other languages gives error if a comment (`#`) is used when knitting a LaTeX doc

messages.author: 980f46a66dfc8362
messages.subject: Highlighting other languages gives error if a comment (`#`) is used when knitting a LaTeX doc
parts:
Hi,
Not sure if this is a local problem or a reproducible one but if I write a chunk in bash or python and include a comment, LaTeX will give an error related to the highlighting app.

The original example code parses fine:

\documentclass{article}
\begin{document}
Syntax highlighting also works for other languages in the \LaTeX{} or HTML output, if Highlight has been installed (and is in PATH).
<<hi-python, engine='python'>>=
x = 'hello, python world!'
print x
print x.split(' ')
@
\end{document}

But given a comment


\documentclass{article}
\begin{document}
Syntax highlighting also works for other languages in the \LaTeX{} or HTML output, if Highlight has been installed (and is in PATH).
<<hi-python, engine='python'>>=
# comment
x = 'hello, python world!'
print x
print x.split(' ')
@
\end{document}

I get:

! Undefined control sequence.

l.60 \hlstd{}\hlslc

{\#\ comment}\hspace*{\fill}\\

[1] (./test.aux) )


Same goes for bash, haven't tried other languages, but I assume that any language which uses # to indicate comment will give and error.


Any idea why this is happening?


Roey

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Highlighting other languages gives error if a comment (`#`) is used when knitting a LaTeX doc
parts:
It is a knitr bug, and I will fix it in the next version of knitr. It
is also fairly easy for you to fix it right now by adding

\let\hlesc\hlstd \let\hlpps\hlstd \let\hllin\hlstd \let\hlslc\hlcom

to your LaTeX preamble. Thanks!

Regards,
Yihui
--
Yihui Xie <xiey...@gmail.com>
Web: http://yihui.name
